cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T2 directly: westerlies would carry frigid air without the ocean's heat.
cells.limitation: T3 and T9 float above the exchange; T7 changes topic without answering T6.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 adds blocking highs diverting westerlies, a distinction absent from the openings.
cells.limitation: T3, T6, T9 repeat 'integrated whole' without adding any mechanism; T5's blocking point never reused.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T1-T5 examine ocean heat source versus atmospheric delivery.
cells.limitation: Nobody raises Rocky Mountain stationary waves or continental versus maritime exposure of eastern Canada.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T10 recasts the ocean as fuel tank for the atmospheric engine.
cells.limitation: T10 converges on T6's 'integrated machine' without any argument forcing it; agreement looks scripted.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D: ocean provides heat, atmosphere delivers it.
cells.limitation: T12's storage-versus-rate crux is muddled and does not sharpen the physical question.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 states T2's westerlies claim accurately before answering it.
cells.limitation: T6 says the Oceanographer ignores feedback; T10 drops a 'sole driver' claim T1 never made.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 names the assumption: without ocean heat, westerlies carry frigid air.
cells.limitation: No objection tests ocean transport against the mild Pacific coast or the Rockies' wind pattern.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T5's point that blocking highs bring European cold spells is accurate.
cells.limitation: T11 says the ocean carries the bulk of heat (suspected inaccurate); Taylor's management book misfits climate.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T8 flags correlation versus causation in reading SST maps.
cells.limitation: T1 and T11 state contested primacy as settled; T9 offers a motive guess about the minds.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T5 concedes the ocean stores heat before qualifying its role.
cells.limitation: T10 retracts a claim never made, a goalpost move; no turn names what changed its mind.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A frames the question as ocean currents versus atmospheric circulation.
cells.limitation: T12 and Section E recast the explanation as which measure the user prefers.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: Section A restates the user's latitude comparison.
cells.limitation: No turn names which European and Canadian places, or west versus east coast.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T7 offers a data check suited to someone seeking an explanation.
cells.limitation: Section E treats the user's goal as choosing a priority rather than understanding the cause.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: No invented context about the user; Section A stays with the stated question.
cells.limitation: T8 invents a time cost for checking maps that the user never raised.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T7 suggests looking at January SST maps.
cells.limitation: Never asks which Canadian region is meant, though Vancouver versus Labrador changes the answer.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T9 suggests a wish for a simple answer, aimed at the minds.
cells.limitation: Nothing offers what the user may want from the explanation; no answerable question.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 questions the single-cause assumption both opening turns share.
cells.limitation: T1 accepts the popular Gulf Stream explanation; the user's likely assumption is never examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T12 distinguishes total energy available from delivery rate.
cells.limitation: T12 frames a physics distinction as a user priority, a misfit for an explanation.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T9 names a possible fear that complexity defeats explanation.
cells.limitation: T9's fear is attributed to the minds as guess; the popular textbook expectation goes unexamined.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E offers two conditional lenses the user can accept or reject.
cells.limitation: The lenses in Section E are muddled, so the user has little to refine.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: T1, T2, T3 define ocean transport, westerlies, and coupled explanations.
cells.limitation: Topographic stationary waves and continental exposure are missing from the candidate explanations.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T8 notes SST maps risk mistaking correlation for causation.
cells.limitation: No turn states what evidence each explanation predicts or what would embarrass it.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: T7 proposes comparing January SST maps with air temperature anomalies.
cells.limitation: T12 ends on which measure the user prefers; Section E's velocity comparison decides nothing.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T5 shows blocking can override ocean warmth in a given winter.
cells.limitation: Major unknowns are not separated from minor ones; Section D leaves primacy vaguely open.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T7's map comparison is a concrete, proportionate thing to look at.
cells.limitation: Section E's heat-capacity and velocity research would not settle between the explanations.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1 and T2 explain current and westerlies in plain terms.
cells.limitation: T11 'forcing agent' and T10 'coupling' go undefined.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4 and T6 name the speaker whose claim they answer.
cells.limitation: T10's 'sole driver' claim traces to no turn; T12 'This depends' has no clear antecedent.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Twelve turns, all within the word range, per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: T7-T8 detour into data-filtering cost slows the middle.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Ocean, atmosphere and systems positions stay distinct through T11.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one flat register and similar turn lengths.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: T5 adds blocking patterns in one sentence.
cells.limitation: T3, T6, T9 repeat the whole-system point; Section E repeats Section D.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T4-T5 contest heat source versus delivery as a real dispute.
cells.limitation: Tension stays abstract; no vivid contrast like Bergen versus Labrador gives it bite.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T10 Oceanographer shifts to coupling.
cells.limitation: T10's reversal names no earlier argument as cause and retracts a claim never made.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T6 'I would go further than Taylor here' hints at a voice.
cells.limitation: No Carson lyricism or distinct character; T3 and T9 hedge in generic terms.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T10: the ocean as fuel tank for the atmospheric engine.
cells.limitation: One apt analogy only; no vivid example of a place or winter.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T5's blocking point briefly raises the stakes of the dispute.
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm and intensity across T1-T12; the ending in T12 deflates.

strengths: T4-T5 exchange gives a genuine objection and answer: ocean heat storage versus atmospheric delivery and blocking.
Section D states a coherent division of roles: the ocean supplies heat, the atmosphere delivers it.
T7 offers a concrete thing to look at, and T10's fuel-tank analogy is clear; language is plain throughout.
weaknesses: T1-T12 never raise Rocky Mountain stationary waves or continental versus maritime exposure, the factors central to this contrast.
T11 and Section E claim the ocean carries the bulk of heat, suspected inaccurate at these latitudes.
T12 and Section E recast the explanation as a user priority; the Systems Thinker (Taylor) adds only generic holism and T10's reversal is uncaused.

symptoms.observed: Never raises Rockies-driven wind patterns or eastern Canada's continental exposure versus Europe's maritime one.
symptoms.evidence: the prevailing westerlies are what actually force that warmed air

symptoms.observed: States the ocean carries most heat; atmosphere likely dominates poleward transport at these latitudes.
symptoms.evidence: the ocean carries the bulk of the heat

symptoms.observed: Adopts the popular Gulf Stream explanation without examining it as the user's likely assumption.
symptoms.evidence: The primary reason for this temperature difference is the North Atlantic Drift

symptoms.observed: Ends on which measure the user prefers, not an observable fact deciding between explanations.
symptoms.evidence: you must decide if you are measuring the total energy available

symptoms.observed: Reversal cites no earlier argument and retracts a claim nobody made.
symptoms.evidence: I drop the claim that the current is the sole driver

findings.description: Claims the ocean carries the bulk of the heat; at roughly 45-60N atmospheric transport is generally thought to dominate, and much research attributes the contrast to stationary atmospheric waves and seasonal ocean heat release.

findings.location: Section B; T3, T6, T9, T12
findings.description: Taylor's The Principles of Scientific Management concerns industrial management, not complex-systems or climate reasoning; the basis does not fit the claims made.
Overstates that without westerlies Europe would be just as frozen as Canada; ignores continental versus maritime exposure and ocean proximity.
Attributions to Carson's The Sea Around Us and Watts's The Weather Handbook could not be checked against source text.

rubric_fit_notes: The question carries no personal context, so C3 and C4 have little to work with; ratings reflect missed opportunities like asking which regions are compared. The scientific-accuracy finding on T11 rests on evaluator knowledge and is reported as suspected only.
question_type_note: Read as exploratory: C4 as examination of the user's likely Gulf Stream assumption, C5 as settling between explanations, penalising T12 and Section E for ending on a user preference.
